page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5.16xlarge is a storage- and memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed under the Local SSDs server family on KVM hypervisors. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors running at a base clock frequency of 3.4 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated virtual cores. To support high-memory operations, the configuration includes 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. There are no discrete GPU accelerators provisioned on this server type.

A primary architectural feature of the ecs.i5.16xlarge is its bundled high-capacity local storage subsystem, providing 15358 GB of direct-attached solid-state disk storage. For network input and output, the instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 160 Gbps to support high-throughput cluster interconnects and data ingestion. It includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating exclusively within configured virtual private networks for external traffic routing.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, bundling over 15 TB of direct-attached SSD storage alongside dense memory eliminates remote storage latency and external volume overhead for input/output intensive architectures. A structural tradeoff of direct-attached storage is the need for application-level data redundancy across nodes to handle host maintenance events. This balanced combination of high vCPU density, 512 GB of memory, and fast local SSD storage aligns directly with distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational databases, search indexing engines, and large-scale analytical processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5.16xlarge is a high-density, storage-oriented virtual machine instance within the Local SSDs family, executed on a KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz. Memory capacity reaches 512 GB, providing an 8.0 GB allocation per virtual core. Storage is provided through an integrated 15358 GB local SSD array, eliminating network-attached storage latency for heavy disk operations. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 160 Gbps, though no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Without hardware GPU acceleration, resource density is concentrated strictly in high-throughput local disk, memory capacity, and processing cores. This infrastructure configuration is designed for write-heavy relational databases, massive distributed NoSQL clusters, search indexing services, in-memory caches backed by local flash, and big data analytics pipelines.
